items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: When I worked with Edmund with Louis he was talking about this story.

ctx.x: About six. Bands were -- no bands in those days had over six or seven pieces. If you had eight, nine pieces you had a real big band in those days. But they were five, six pieces -- like that because later on Edmund
Hall played with Eagle-Eye Shields, and so did -- so did Cootie Williams. This is way back.
